roeAllowAccountLockout.meaning: Whether a technique that can lock a real account out is permitted. Off keeps credential attacks to a single attempt per account. After creation this may only go true to false.

roeAllowDataExfiltration.meaning: Whether a finding may be proven by moving data off the target. Off means the out-of-band callback paths and collector egress are refused at scan start. After creation this may only go true to false.

roeAllowDos.meaning: Whether denial-of-service techniques are permitted. Off means the DoS module and every aggression switch that could exhaust a target are refused at scan start, whatever their own toggles say. After creation this may only go true to false.

roeAllowPhysicalAccess.meaning: Whether the engagement covers physical access. Recorded for the report; the pipeline has no physical capability. After creation this may only go true to false.

roeAllowProductionTesting.meaning: Whether production systems are in scope. Off is a statement the operator makes about the estate, not something the scanner can verify, so it constrains what an agent may choose rather than what a tool can reach.

roeAllowSocialEngineering.meaning: Whether techniques aimed at people rather than systems are permitted. After creation this may only go true to false.

roeDocumentMimeType.meaning: The media type of the uploaded Rules of Engagement document.

roeEmergencyContact.meaning: Who to reach out of hours if a scan causes an incident.

roeEnabled.meaning: The master switch for the Rules of Engagement. While it is off there is NO rate ceiling at all, whatever roeGlobalMaxRps says, because the capper is gated on this flag. After creation it may only go false to true.

roeEngagementEndDate.meaning: The last date the engagement authorises any activity.

roeEngagementStartDate.meaning: The first date the engagement authorises any activity.

roeEngagementType.meaning: How the engagement is classified in the report: pentest, bug bounty, red team and so on.

roeExcludedHostReasons.meaning: Why each excluded host is excluded, keyed by host. Read by the report; it does not itself exclude anything.

roeExcludedHosts.meaning: Hosts that must never be touched even though they fall inside the target scope. After creation this may only grow: an agent that discovers a new exclusion applies it immediately, and one that wants to remove an exclusion asks a human.

roeForbiddenTools.meaning: Tools that may not run on this engagement, by name, whatever their own enable flag says. Enforced at scan start. After creation this list may only grow.

roeGlobalMaxRps.meaning: The engagement's request-rate ceiling, in requests per second. Every per-tool rate is capped to it at scan start, including the ones whose own value means 'unlimited'. ZERO MEANS NO CEILING, so a project with roeEnabled on and this at 0 is not rate-limited. After creation it may only decrease, and never back to 0 once it is non-zero.

roeIncidentProcedure.meaning: What to do if the engagement causes an outage or a security incident.

roeMaxSeverityPhase.meaning: The most severe phase the engagement permits, which bounds how far an attack chain may be taken. After creation it may only move toward the less severe end.

roeNotes.meaning: Free-text engagement notes that did not fit another field.

roeParsedJson.meaning: The structured form extracted from the uploaded document, which populated the fields above.

roeRawText.meaning: The Rules of Engagement document as plain text, kept so the report can quote it.

roeRequireDataEncryption.meaning: Whether engagement data must be encrypted at rest.

roeSensitiveDataHandling.meaning: The agreed handling rule for sensitive data encountered during the engagement.

roeStatusUpdateFrequency.meaning: How often the client expects a progress update during the engagement.

roeThirdPartyProviders.meaning: Third-party providers hosting in-scope assets, who may need their own notification.

roeTimeWindowDays.meaning: Days of the week on which scanning is permitted.

roeTimeWindowEnabled.meaning: Whether scanning is restricted to an agreed time window.

roeTimeWindowEndTime.meaning: Local end of the permitted scanning window, as HH:MM.

roeTimeWindowStartTime.meaning: Local start of the permitted scanning window, as HH:MM.

roeTimeWindowTimezone.meaning: The IANA timezone the scanning window's times are read in.

shodanReverseDns.meaning: Asks Shodan for the names an IP is known by, which often reveals hosts DNS enumeration missed.

sqliTamperScripts.meaning: Comma-separated SQLMap tamper scripts for WAF bypass. Leave empty for auto-detection.

ssrfOobCallbackEnabled.meaning: Whether ssrf runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

ssrfOobProvider.meaning: interactsh-client server. Use a self-hosted instance if oast.fun is blocked.

ssrfPayloadReferenceEnabled.meaning: Whether ssrf runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

ssrfPortScanPorts.meaning: Comma-separated ports to probe via SSRF. Trim for quieter scans, extend for thorough coverage.

ssrfRequestTimeout.meaning: How long ssrf may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

stealthMode.meaning: Reduce scan aggressiveness and network noise

subdomainList.meaning: Hosts seeded into the scan in addition to whatever discovery finds. Part of the engagement scope, so it is write-once. Empty entries are dropped and every entry is whitespace-stripped at load.

subfinderDockerImage.meaning: The container image spawned for subfinder. Any value outside the shipped allowlist is silently pinned back to the default at scan start, with a [guardrail] line recording it, so the field is open and the runtime is the control.

subfinderEnabled.meaning: Whether subfinder runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

subfinderMaxResults.meaning: Maximum subdomains taken from a subfinder run.

subjackAll.meaning: Test every URL, not just identified CNAMEs - slower (default false)

subjackCheckAr.meaning: Detect stale A records pointing to dead cloud IPs (manual review)

subjackCheckNs.meaning: Detect NS takeovers (expired nameservers / dangling cloud DNS delegations)

subjackEnabled.meaning: Whether subjack runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

subjackRunTimeout.meaning: How long subjack may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

subjackSsl.meaning: Force HTTPS probing for higher accuracy (default true)

subjackThreads.meaning: How many subjack operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

subjackTimeout.meaning: How long subjack may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

supplyChainDeepAnalysisEnabled.meaning: Whether Supply chain scan runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

supplyChainEcosystems.meaning: Package ecosystems the supply-chain scan analyses, such as npm, pypi or go.

supplyChainInputMode.meaning: Whether the supply-chain scan reads an uploaded SBOM, a repository, or an organisation.

supplyChainOrgDeepAnalysisEnabled.meaning: Whether Supply chain scan runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

supplyChainOrgIncludeArchived.meaning: Whether archived repositories are included when scanning an organisation.

supplyChainOrgIncludeForks.meaning: Whether forked repositories are included when scanning an organisation.

supplyChainOrgMaxRepos.meaning: Maximum repositories walked when scanning an organisation.

supplyChainOrgName.meaning: The GitHub organisation whose repositories the supply-chain scan walks. Points the scanner at someone else's assets, so it is write-once.

supplyChainOrgRef.meaning: The git ref checked out in each organisation repository, when one is pinned.

supplyChainReconDeepAnalysisEnabled.meaning: Whether Supply chain recon runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

supplyChainReconEcosystems.meaning: Comma-separated OSV ecosystems to report (default "npm"). Matched EXACTLY against the harvested package ecosystem, so use these names verbatim, case included: npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, crates.io, Packagist, RubyGems, NuGet. Empty string means no filter (report every ecosystem)

supplyChainReconEnabled.meaning: Whether Supply chain recon runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

supplyChainRepoRef.meaning: The git ref checked out in the scanned repository. Write-once with the repository it belongs to.

supplyChainRepoScope.meaning: Which parts of the repository the scan reads. Write-once with the repository it belongs to.

supplyChainRepoUrl.meaning: The repository the supply-chain scan clones. It becomes a git clone argument against a third party's infrastructure, so it is write-once like the scope.

supplyChainSbomFile.meaning: The uploaded SBOM this project analyses. Written only by the upload endpoint, which also places the file on disk; a second writer could name a file the project never uploaded.

supplyChainTyposquatEnabled.meaning: Whether Supply chain scan runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

takeoverAiClassifier.meaning: Use AI to disambiguate takeover findings from WAF "no host" block pages that match the same static fingerprint (requires aiInPipeline=true). For each finding the scanner probes the host, short-circuits on third-party vendor tokens, and otherwise asks the LLM to classify the body. AI-flagged collisions get score -40 (lands in manual_review). Default false.

takeoverCertValidationEnabled.meaning: Whether takeover runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

takeoverConfidenceThreshold.meaning: 0..100. Findings >= threshold+10 are confirmed, >= threshold are likely, otherwise manual_review

takeoverManualReviewAutoPublish.meaning: Publish manual_review findings into the main Vulnerability stream (default false)

takeoverRateLimit.meaning: Requests per second takeover sends. Capped to the engagement ceiling at scan start, so a value above the ceiling is rewritten rather than refused.

takeoverSeverity.meaning: Severity filter for Nuclei takeover templates (e.g. ["critical","high","medium"])

targetDomain.meaning: The single root domain this engagement covers. THE scope column: every phase derives its hosts from it and the target guardrail measures against it. Set once at creation and immutable afterwards, because changing it on an existing project turns a rescan credential into one aimed at a third party. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped at load.

targetGuardrailEnabled.meaning: The hard guardrail that refuses to scan a host outside the declared scope. Turning it off removes the control that keeps the pipeline inside its engagement, which is why it moves with the scope and cannot change on an existing project.

targetIps.meaning: The IP addresses or CIDR ranges scanned when ipMode is on. Part of the engagement scope, so it is write-once. Empty entries are dropped and every entry is stripped at load.

tlsxCipherConcurrency.meaning: How many tlsx operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

tlsxCipherEnum.meaning: Enumerate weak supported ciphers (extra connections per target). Default false.

tlsxConcurrency.meaning: How many tlsx operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

tlsxDelay.meaning: Optional -delay between connections (e.g. "200ms"); stealth only. Default "".

tlsxDockerImage.meaning: The container image spawned for tlsx. Any value outside the shipped allowlist is silently pinned back to the default at scan start, with a [guardrail] line recording it, so the field is open and the runtime is the control.

tlsxEnabled.meaning: Whether tlsx runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

tlsxIncludeHttpPorts.meaning: Also grab certs on HTTP/HTTPS ports httpx already covers (duplicate handshakes). Default false.

tlsxInjectHostnames.meaning: Merge in-scope certificate SAN hostnames into dns.subdomains as new probe targets. Default true.

tlsxMaxHostnamesPerIp.meaning: When one IP serves several known hostnames, how many to scan (each may present a different cert). Default 1.

tlsxMaxInjectedHostnames.meaning: Cap on in-scope certificate SAN hostnames merged back into dns.subdomains as scan targets. Default 200.

tlsxMaxTargets.meaning: Hard cap on ip:port pairs tlsx scans. Default 2000.

tlsxProbeJarm.meaning: Compute JARM + JA3 fingerprints (~10 extra handshakes per target, loud). Default false.

tlsxRetries.meaning: How many times tlsx retries a failed request before giving up on it.

tlsxRevPtrSni.meaning: Reverse-PTR to derive an SNI for bare IPs (extra DNS lookups). Default false.

tlsxRunTimeout.meaning: How long tlsx may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

tlsxTimeout.meaning: How long tlsx may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

tlsxVersionEnum.meaning: Enumerate every supported TLS version (extra connections per target). Default false.

triageReviewBudget.meaning: How many findings one triage job may review before it stops and reports what it got through.

trufflehogAllowVerificationOverlap.meaning: Whether several detectors may verify the same candidate, which costs requests but catches more.

trufflehogArchiveMaxDepth.meaning: How many nested archives are extracted before the scan stops descending.

trufflehogArchiveMaxSize.meaning: The largest archive extracted, in bytes. A larger one is skipped rather than exhausting the container.

trufflehogArchiveTimeout.meaning: Seconds one archive extraction may take before it is abandoned.

trufflehogConcurrency.meaning: How many sources trufflehog scans at once.

trufflehogDetectorTimeout.meaning: Seconds one detector may spend verifying a candidate before it is abandoned.

trufflehogDropUnverifiedJwt.meaning: Discards JWTs that could not be verified, which are the bulk of the false positives in this class.

trufflehogEnabled.meaning: Whether trufflehog runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

trufflehogExcludeDetectors.meaning: Detectors that never run, whatever the include list says.

trufflehogFilterEntropy.meaning: The Shannon entropy below which a candidate string is discarded before detection runs.

trufflehogForceSkipArchives.meaning: Skips archives entirely rather than extracting them, which is faster and misses anything inside.

trufflehogForceSkipBinaries.meaning: Skips binary files rather than scanning them for embedded strings.

trufflehogIncludeDetectors.meaning: Restricts the run to these detectors. Empty means every detector runs.

trufflehogMaxDecodeDepth.meaning: How many nested encodings are unwrapped before giving up on a candidate.

trufflehogNoVerification.meaning: Skip live verification entirely. When set, every finding lands `unverified` (never checked), which is NOT the same as "not live".

trufflehogResultTypes.meaning: Which result statuses to report: a comma-separated subset of verified,unverified,unknown,filtered_unverified. Replaces the old trufflehogOnlyVerified boolean, which combined with trufflehogNoVerification asked TruffleHog to report only verified results while forbidding it to verify — zero findings, no error.

uncoverEnabled.meaning: Whether uncover runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

uncoverMaxResults.meaning: The most results uncover accumulates in one pass. The memory governor budgets it against available RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

updateGraphDb.meaning: Store results in the graph database

updatedAt.meaning: When the project row last changed. Written by the database on every update.

updatedById.meaning: The user who last updated the project. Populated going forward only; may be null on older rows.

urlscanMaxResults.meaning: The most results urlscan accumulates in one pass. The memory governor budgets it against available RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

useBruteforceForSubdomains.meaning: Enable DNS brute-force for subdomain discovery

userId.meaning: The owning user. Writing it reassigns the project to someone else and configures nothing, which is why it is closed on every surface.

verifyDomainOwnership.meaning: Requires a DNS TXT record proving control of the target before any active phase runs. Part of the scope's proof, so it is write-once.

vhostSniBaselineSizeTolerance.meaning: Body size deltas within this many bytes are not flagged (suppresses Set-Cookie / timestamp jitter). Default 50.

vhostSniConcurrency.meaning: How many Vhost / SNI enumeration operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

vhostSniCustomWordlist.meaning: Optional newline-separated custom prefixes/hostnames (per-project file/text). Bare prefixes expand as {prefix}.{target_apex}; full hostnames are used as-is. Default "".

vhostSniEnabled.meaning: Whether Vhost / SNI enumeration runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

vhostSniInjectDiscovered.meaning: When a hidden vhost is confirmed, create a BaseURL node so a follow-up partial recon (Katana, Nuclei) can scan it. Default true.

vhostSniMaxCandidatesPerIp.meaning: Hard cap on candidates per IP to bound run time. Default 2000.

vhostSniTestL4.meaning: Run the TLS SNI trick via curl --resolve (catches modern reverse proxies, k8s ingress, Cloudflare). Default true.

vhostSniTestL7.meaning: Run the HTTP Host header trick (catches classic Apache/Nginx vhosts). Default true.

vhostSniTimeout.meaning: How long Vhost / SNI enumeration may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

vhostSniUseDefaultWordlist.meaning: Use the bundled vhost-common.txt wordlist (~2,300 admin/dev/staging/internal/modern-stack prefixes, expanded as {prefix}.{target_apex}). Default true.

vhostSniUseGraphCandidates.meaning: Pull hostnames from existing Subdomain, ExternalDomain, TLS SAN list, CNAME targets and reverse-DNS PTR records resolving to each target IP. Highest signal source. Default true.

virusTotalWorkers.meaning: How many virustotal operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

wafAiClassifier.meaning: Use AI to classify WAF/CDN presence from response headers/body/latency when the static check misses (requires aiInPipeline=true). Augments _has_cdn_markers and check_waf_bypass; AI-detected bypasses are tagged detection_method=ai_classifier. Default false.

wappalyzerAutoUpdate.meaning: Wappalyzer package version for tech database

wappalyzerCacheTtlHours.meaning: How long to cache tech database (0 = always fresh)

wappalyzerEnabled.meaning: Whether wappalyzer runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

wappalyzerMinConfidence.meaning: The confidence percentage below which a Wappalyzer technology match is discarded.

wappalyzerNpmVersion.meaning: The npm version of Wappalyzer the scan container installs at run time. It is fetched from the public registry during the scan, so it decides what code runs inside the container.

wappalyzerRequireHtml.meaning: Whether a technology match requires an HTML response, which suppresses matches on JSON and binary endpoints.

webCachePoisonAllowCpdos.meaning: Cache-poisoned DoS tests (oversized/meta-char). Only honored in research profile. Default false.

webCachePoisonAllowDeception.meaning: Web cache deception (path-confusion .css tricks). Default true.

webCachePoisonAllowFrameworkPacks.meaning: Fire Next.js/Nuxt/Remix-specific vectors only when the tech fingerprint matches. Default true.

webCachePoisonBehavioralDelay.meaning: Seconds to wait between the two frozen-Date probes. Larger = more reliable on slow origins, but adds latency per silent URL. Default 1.1.

webCachePoisonBehavioralOracle.meaning: Detect *silent* caches (no cache-status headers, common with default Varnish/nginx or hardened CDNs) via a frozen-Date probe: fetch twice across a short delay; a frozen Date header + identical body implies a cache. Catches caches header detection alone would miss. Default true.

webCachePoisonCacheBusterParam.meaning: Query param name used to isolate every test into its own cache slot. Default "rdmncb".

webCachePoisonCacheHeader.meaning: Override the cache hit/miss header if the target uses a non-standard one. Default "".

webCachePoisonConcurrency.meaning: How many Web cache poisoning operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

webCachePoisonConfirmWorkers.meaning: How many Web cache poisoning operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

webCachePoisonCrossVantage.meaning: Re-confirm from a second network vantage (requires extra egress infra). Default false.

webCachePoisonDifferential.meaning: Non-reflective detection. Beyond looking for a benign canary echoed back, also flag a poison that changes the response *behaviour* (a persisted status code / Location redirect / body) with no echoed marker, guarded against false positives by requiring the affected response dimension to be stable across two clean baselines. Catches CPDoS-style status flips, scheme/redirect poisoning, and cache-key confusion. Adds one extra baseline request per vector. Default true.

webCachePoisonDockerImage.meaning: The container image spawned for Web cache poisoning. Any value outside the shipped allowlist is silently pinned back to the default at scan start, with a [guardrail] line recording it, so the field is open and the runtime is the control.

webCachePoisonEnabled.meaning: Whether Web cache poisoning runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

webCachePoisonMaxRpsPerHost.meaning: Requests per second the web-cache-poisoning scan sends to any ONE host. ZERO MEANS UNLIMITED, so 0 is the most aggressive value available and not the safest. Under an engagement ceiling a 0 here is rewritten to the ceiling at scan start.

webCachePoisonMinConfidence.meaning: Only findings scoring at or above this (0-1) become Vulnerability nodes. 0.8 keeps Confirmed + Strong. Default 0.8.

webCachePoisonScanProfile.meaning: "safe-confirm" (production, benign canaries, always isolated), "extended" (owned test targets), or "research" (lab only, enables CPDoS if allowed). Default "safe-confirm".

webCachePoisonTimeout.meaning: How long Web cache poisoning may spend before it is abandoned, in seconds. A run that hits it contributes whatever it found so far rather than failing the scan.

webCachePoisonTimeoutPerReq.meaning: Native confirmation per-request timeout in seconds. Default 10.

webCachePoisonVerifySsl.meaning: Verify TLS certificates during native confirmation. Default true.

whoisEnabled.meaning: Whether whois runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

whoisMaxRetries.meaning: How many times whois retries a failed request before giving up on it.

zapAjaxSpiderDockerImage.meaning: The container image spawned for zap. Any value outside the shipped allowlist is silently pinned back to the default at scan start, with a [guardrail] line recording it, so the field is open and the runtime is the control.

zapAjaxSpiderEnabled.meaning: Whether zap runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

zapAjaxSpiderEventWait.meaning: How long the Ajax Spider waits after firing a DOM event, in MILLISECONDS. Too low and a single-page app has not rendered its new state before the crawler reads it.

zapAjaxSpiderExcludePatterns.meaning: Regex patterns to exclude from Ajax crawling

zapAjaxSpiderLogoutAvoidance.meaning: Avoid actions likely to log out

zapAjaxSpiderMaxCrawlStates.meaning: Max crawl states, or 0 for unlimited

zapAjaxSpiderMaxDuration.meaning: How long the ZAP Ajax Spider may crawl one seed, in MINUTES rather than seconds.

zapAjaxSpiderMaxUrls.meaning: The most results zap accumulates in one pass. The memory governor budgets it against available RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

zapAjaxSpiderNumberOfBrowsers.meaning: Browser instances used by Ajax Spider

zapAjaxSpiderParallelism.meaning: How many zap operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

zapAjaxSpiderReloadWait.meaning: How long the Ajax Spider waits after a page reload, in MILLISECONDS.

zoomEyeEnabled.meaning: Whether ZoomEye runs. Configuration is two levels: this flag decides whether the tool runs INSIDE its phase, and scanModules decides whether the phase runs at all. Setting one without the other is a silent no-op.

zoomEyeMaxResults.meaning: The most results ZoomEye accumulates in one pass. The memory governor budgets it against available RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

zoomEyeWorkers.meaning: How many ZoomEye operations run at once. The memory governor scales it down when the host is short of RAM, so the effective value can be below what is written here.

AUTH_PROFILE.meaning: The authenticated session the scan replays: cookies, headers and the login steps that produced them. Deliberately a RELATION rather than a Project column, because GET /api/projects/[id] spreads every Project scalar to the browser and a credential stored as a column would leak. It arrives in the same API payload the settings load reads, so the pipeline sees it as a runtime key with no column behind it.
